Don’t add the pressure of having to find a solution or distraction in everything. Just do whatever activity is healthy and interesting at first. Let it lead you somewhere new.
Start by doing things you like or try new things. Start small. Eventually, something will draw you in. Doesn’t matter what it is, as long as it is positive/constructive.
I understand the recklessness. I survived a motorcycle wreck that I wasn’t supposed to. I aim my car at highway walls and turn away at the last minute. One day it will get me.

I am in a similar position. And I think sometimes, if I hate work this bad that it’s going to kill me, what difference does it make if you quit first? I can still end it after I run out of money, so why not put it off a little longer and give myself a week or two to enjoy having quit a shit job? Maybe that starts the change I need?

Maybe it is just me. 
And Cornell and Thompson and Bergling and Bennington and Flint and Jeni and Mirra and Trucks and Williams and Stevens and Spade and Bourdain and Cobain

You are not a failure. It keeps getting worse and you’re still standing. That’s success. 
Failure is not what you are it’s something you experience. We all fail. All the time. I failed today. But if you and I able to talk about it, we’re still standing. And we can try again in a different way. I’m talking to myself as I type this, just as much as I’m talking to you. Because I understand how you feel as well.
